cases.name: lease_basics_1
cases.objective: For a tenant considering early exit, identify the contractual break dates, notice requirements, break premium and stated term expiry. Do not determine whether conditions are satisfied.

findings.title: Break Dates
findings.interpretation: The tenant has two contractual break dates on which the lease may be terminated early: the fifth anniversary (1 January 2029) and the tenth anniversary (1 January 2034) of the term commencement. These are the only dates on which the tenant may exercise break rights.
findings.relevance: Essential for tenant planning early exit strategy; identifies the specific calendar dates available for lease termination.
findings.next_step: Confirm current date and calculate which break date is applicable. Verify whether the lease remains in force and no prior break has been exercised.
findings.quote: The Tenant may determine this Lease on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2029) or the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2034) (each a "Break Date") by serving written notice on the Landlord in accordance with clause 8.2.
findings.uncertainty: None regarding the break dates themselves as stated in the lease. Uncertainty exists as to whether conditions for exercise have been satisfied.

findings.title: Notice Requirement for Break Exercise
findings.interpretation: The tenant must provide a minimum of 12 months' prior written notice before the break date. Once served, the break notice becomes irrevocable. Service must comply with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (as amended).
findings.relevance: Critical procedural requirement. The tenant must plan backwards from the desired break date by at least 12 months to meet notice obligations. Failure to serve timely notice prevents break exercise.
findings.next_step: Verify that any break notice, if intended, is served at least 12 months before the desired break date and confirm compliance with Section 196 service provisions.
findings.quote: The Tenant must give the Landlord not less than twelve (12) months' prior written notice of its intention to exercise a break right (a "Break Notice"). A Break Notice, once given, shall be irrevocable. Any Break Notice must be served in accordance with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (as amended).
findings.uncertainty: The specific service mechanics under Section 196 are not reproduced in the lease and require reference to that statute.

findings.title: Break Premium
findings.interpretation: The tenant must pay the landlord a break premium equal to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the break date. This payment must be made in cleared funds on or before the break date and is a mandatory condition of break exercise.
findings.relevance: Material financial obligation. The current rent payable determines the break premium amount. Initial rent is £850,000 per annum, but rent may have been reviewed upward on 1 January 2029 or 1 January 2034 depending on which break date applies.
findings.next_step: Establish the current rent rate payable immediately before the intended break date. Calculate the break premium as half of the annual rent rate then in effect. Prepare cleared funds transfer on or before break date.
findings.quote: the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date (the "Break Premium"), such payment to be made by way of cleared funds.
findings.uncertainty: The actual break premium amount depends on the rent review outcome at the fifth or tenth anniversary, which involves open market valuation by an independent surveyor. Current rent rate is not determinable without knowing the review date applied.

findings.title: Stated Term Expiry
findings.interpretation: The lease term is for 15 years commencing on 1 January 2024 and expiring on 31 December 2038, unless earlier terminated in accordance with lease provisions (including break exercise). This is the natural expiry date absent exercise of break rights.
findings.relevance: Establishes the baseline lease duration and ultimate expiry date. If no break is exercised, the lease continues to 31 December 2038. Early exit via break avoids remaining lease obligations beyond the break date.
findings.next_step: Confirm that the lease has not been earlier terminated and that the tenant intends to determine the lease before the natural expiry of 31 December 2038.
findings.quote: The Term shall be for a period of fifteen (15) years commencing on 1 January 2024 and expiring on 31 December 2038, subject to earlier determination in accordance with the provisions of this Lease.
findings.uncertainty: None as to the stated expiry date itself. The phrase "subject to earlier determination" confirms that break exercise can shorten the term, but does not create conditions or uncertainty about the expiry date.

findings.title: Conditions for Break Exercise
findings.interpretation: Break exercise is conditional on three matters being satisfied on or before the relevant break date: (a) no material breach of tenant covenants remains unremedied; (b) vacant possession is delivered free from all occupiers and subtenants; (c) break premium is paid. Failure of any condition renders the break notice of no effect and the lease continues.
findings.relevance: The tenant must satisfy all three conditions to successfully exit on a break date. Non-compliance with any condition prevents termination.
findings.next_step: Audit tenant's compliance with lease covenants; identify any outstanding breaches and remediation status. Confirm no subtenancies or third-party occupancy. Ensure break premium funds are prepared. Do not assess whether conditions are satisfied; report only on the stated conditions.
findings.quote: The Tenant's right to determine this Lease on a Break Date shall be conditional upon the following conditions being satisfied on or before the relevant Break Date: (a) there is no material breach by the Tenant of any of the Tenant's covenants in this Lease which remains unremedied at the Break Date; (b) the Tenant gives vacant possession of the whole of the Premises to the Landlord on or before the Break Date, free from all occupiers, subtenants and other persons claiming through or under the Tenant; (c) the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date
findings.uncertainty: The lease does not define 'material breach' and the assessment of materiality and remediation status requires fact-finding. The exact boundaries of vacant possession (common parts, fixtures, chattels) may require interpretation.

findings.title: Initial Rent (not current rent)
findings.interpretation: The initial annual rent is £850,000 per annum exclusive of VAT, payable quarterly in advance on specified quarter days. However, rent is subject to upward-only review on 1 January 2029 and 1 January 2034 (the review dates coinciding with the break dates). The rent payable immediately before each break date will be the relevant reviewed rent, not the initial rent.
findings.relevance: The break premium calculation depends on the current rent immediately before the break date, not the initial rent. On the first break date (1 January 2029), an upward-only rent review will have applied as of that date. On the second break date (1 January 2034), a second upward-only review will have applied. The tenant should not assume the break premium equals £425,000 (six months of initial rent); it will be higher unless the open market rent has remained flat.
findings.next_step: Obtain the reviewed rent determined for 1 January 2029 and/or 1 January 2034, depending on intended break date. Use the reviewed rent to calculate the break premium due.
findings.quote: The Tenant shall pay to the Landlord the Initial Rent of Eight Hundred and Fifty Thousand Pounds (£850,000) per annum, without any deduction, counterclaim or set-off whatsoever
findings.uncertainty: The reviewed rent depends on open market valuation determinations by independent surveyor as of each review date. The final reviewed rent may not be ascertained until after the review date; the lease provides that if not ascertained by the review date, rent continues at the prior rate with a catch-up mechanism.

gaps: No information on whether a break notice has already been served or any prior break exercise attempt.
No current date provided; therefore cannot determine which break date (if any) is pending or has passed.
Current rent rate payable immediately before each break date cannot be determined without knowledge of the reviewed rent outcomes on 1 January 2029 and 1 January 2034.
Status of any material breaches by tenant of lease covenants is not reviewed; compliance with condition (a) for break exercise cannot be assessed from the lease text alone.
No details on whether any subtenancies or third-party occupancies currently exist; compliance with condition (b) cannot be assessed.
No information on whether the tenant intends to exercise the first, second, or neither break date, limiting advice specificity.

cases.draft:
CLIENT UPDATE: EARLY LEASE EXIT – CONTRACTUAL BREAK RIGHTS SUMMARY

BREAK DATES AVAILABLE
The lease permits early termination on two dates only:
- **First break date: 1 January 2029** (fifth anniversary of term commencement)
- **Second break date: 1 January 2034** (tenth anniversary of term commencement)

These are the only dates on which you may exercise a break right. The lease will otherwise expire naturally on 31 December 2038 (being a 15-year term from 1 January 2024). [p.4, p.7]

NOTICE REQUIREMENT
To exercise a break right, you must serve **not less than 12 months' prior written notice** on the Landlord. Once served, this notice becomes irrevocable and cannot be withdrawn. Service must comply with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (as amended). [p.7]

*Practical implication:* To exit on 1 January 2029, notice must be served by 31 December 2027 at the latest. To exit on 1 January 2034, notice must be served by 31 December 2032 at the latest.

BREAK PREMIUM
You must pay the Landlord a **break premium equal to six (6) months' rent** at the rate payable immediately before the break date. This must be paid in cleared funds on or before the break date. [p.7]

*Note on current amount:* The initial rent is £850,000 per annum (exclusive of VAT, payable quarterly in advance). However, rent is subject to upward-only review on 1 January 2029 and again on 1 January 2034. Accordingly, the break premium will be calculated at six months of the **reviewed rent**, not the initial rent. **We need to establish the current rent rate applicable immediately before your intended break date to quantify the premium due.** If the first break date is intended, we require the rent review figure determined for 1 January 2029. [p.4, p.7]

CONDITIONS FOR EXERCISE
Your right to break is conditional. All three conditions below must be satisfied on or before the relevant break date, or the break notice will be of no effect and the lease will continue:

1. **No material breach of tenant covenants:** There must be no material breach of any of your covenants under the lease remaining unremedied at the break date. [p.7]

2. **Vacant possession:** You must deliver vacant possession of the whole of the Premises to the Landlord on or before the break date, free from all occupiers, subtenants and other persons claiming through or under you. [p.7]

3. **Payment of break premium:** You must pay the break premium (as described above) on or before the break date. [p.7]

INFORMATION STILL REQUIRED
To proceed, we need to:
- Confirm today's date and which break date is feasible given notice requirements
- Obtain the reviewed rent figure(s) applicable on 1 January 2029 and/or 1 January 2034 (depending on your intended break date)
- Audit your compliance with lease covenants to identify any unremedied material breaches
- Confirm whether any subtenancies or third-party occupancies exist
- Verify that no prior break notice has already been served

**Please note:** This summary identifies the contractual framework only. We have not assessed whether the conditions for break exercise are satisfied, nor do we confirm your current arrears status or breach history. Those matters require separate fact-finding and will be addressed in our next communication.

---

cases.name: false_premise
cases.objective: Does this lease guarantee the tenant can terminate at any time without penalty? Explain the evidence and any limitations.

findings.title: Break clause limited to specific dates only
findings.interpretation: The lease does NOT guarantee the tenant can terminate at any time without penalty. The tenant has break rights only on two fixed dates: the fifth anniversary (1 January 2029) and tenth anniversary (1 January 2034) of the lease commencement.
findings.relevance: The tenant is locked into a 15-year lease (to 31 December 2038) except for these two narrow windows. Early termination outside these dates is not permitted under the break clause provisions.
findings.next_step: Review whether any other termination provisions exist elsewhere in the lease (not yet examined) or under common law/statute. Check if circumstances have changed materially since lease commencement.
findings.quote: The Tenant may determine this Lease on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2029) or the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2034) (each a "Break Date") by serving written notice on the Landlord
findings.uncertainty: No other termination mechanisms have been reviewed. The lease may contain other provisions elsewhere permitting termination in specific circumstances (e.g. frustration, landlord default, change of law).

findings.title: Break premium penalty required
findings.interpretation: Exercise of the break right is expressly conditioned on payment of a 'Break Premium' equal to six months' rent. This is a significant financial penalty that must be paid on or before the break date to exercise the right.
findings.relevance: Even if the tenant exercises a break right on the permitted date, termination is not 'without penalty'. The tenant must pay 6 months' rent as a condition of escape. If the premium is not paid, the break notice has no effect and the lease continues.
findings.next_step: Determine current rent amount payable to calculate the financial cost of exercising the break right. Clarify whether 'rent' includes service charges and other additional rent or only base rent.
findings.quote: the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date (the "Break Premium"), such payment to be made by way of cleared funds.
findings.uncertainty: Definition of 'rent' for purposes of the break premium calculation. The lease distinguishes between 'yearly rent' (clause 3) and 'additional rent' (clause 2.1(b)). It is unclear whether the break premium covers only base rent or all sums payable as rent.

findings.title: Multiple conditions precedent to break exercise
findings.interpretation: In addition to the 12-month notice requirement and break premium, the tenant must satisfy three conditions: (1) no material unremedied breach of tenant covenants; (2) vacant possession delivered free of occupiers; and (3) payment of break premium. Failure of any condition renders the break notice void.
findings.relevance: The tenant's right to terminate is heavily conditional. Even on the correct date, with correct notice, and with payment, the tenant cannot break if in material breach or if the premises remain occupied. This provides significant leverage to the landlord.
findings.next_step: Review the tenant's covenant obligations throughout the lease to identify material breaches that could prevent break exercise. Consider whether 'vacant possession' requirement has been satisfied if any subtenants remain.
findings.quote: The Tenant's right to determine this Lease on a Break Date shall be conditional upon the following conditions being satisfied on or before the relevant Break Date: (a) there is no material breach by the Tenant of any of the Tenant's covenants in this Lease which remains unremedied at the Break Date; (b) the Tenant gives vacant possession of the whole of the Premises to the Landlord on or before the Break Date, free from all occupiers, subtenants and other persons claiming through or under the Tenant; (c) the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent

findings.title: 12-month advance notice requirement with no flexibility
findings.interpretation: The tenant must serve written notice at least 12 months before the intended break date. Once served, the notice is irrevocable. This means commitment is locked in well in advance, and the tenant cannot change course.
findings.relevance: The tenant cannot wait until close to the break date to decide. A 12-month notice window significantly restricts the tenant's ability to respond to changed circumstances immediately prior to the break date.
findings.next_step: Confirm the notice must be served by the 12-month threshold and cannot be served later, even with consent. Verify the correct service method in accordance with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925.

cases.objective: For a tenant considering early exit, identify the contractual break dates, notice requirements, break premium and stated term expiry. Do not determine whether conditions are satisfied. Also inspect the appendix on the final PDF page as source material.

findings.title: Contractual Break Dates
findings.interpretation: The tenant has two break dates available: the fifth anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (1 January 2029) and the tenth anniversary (1 January 2034). These are the only dates on which the tenant may exercise break rights under Section 8.1.1.
findings.relevance: Essential for tenant considering early exit—identifies the specific dates when break can be exercised without being in breach.
findings.next_step: Determine current date to establish which break date(s) are still available and calculate the time remaining to serve notice.
findings.quote: The Tenant may determine this Lease on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2029) or the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Term Commencement Date (being 1 January 2034) (each a "Break Date") by serving written notice on the Landlord in accordance with clause 8.2.
findings.uncertainty: The document does not indicate whether either break date has already passed or whether the tenant is still within a notice period for a forthcoming break date.

findings.title: Notice Requirement—12 Months Prior Notice
findings.interpretation: The tenant must give the landlord a minimum of twelve (12) months' prior written notice of intention to exercise a break right. Once given, a Break Notice is irrevocable. The notice must comply with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925.
findings.relevance: Critical timing requirement for tenant exit planning. Failure to give proper notice will result in loss of break rights.
findings.next_step: Verify the exact service requirements under Section 196 LPA 1925 and determine the date by which notice must be served to trigger a particular break date.
findings.quote: The Tenant must give the Landlord not less than twelve (12) months' prior written notice of its intention to exercise a break right (a "Break Notice"). A Break Notice, once given, shall be irrevocable. Any Break Notice must be served in accordance with Section 196 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (as amended).
findings.uncertainty: Document does not specify what form the notice must take or confirm receipt procedures. Section 196 LPA 1925 service rules must be separately reviewed.

findings.title: Break Premium—Six Months' Rent Payable
findings.interpretation: To exercise a break right, the tenant must pay to the landlord a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date. This payment must be made by cleared funds on or before the Break Date and is a condition for effective exercise of the break.
findings.relevance: Significant financial cost associated with early exit—tenant must budget for payment of six months' rent as a condition of break exercise, in addition to vacating possession.
findings.next_step: Calculate the current rent payable under the lease to establish the quantum of the Break Premium payable. Verify whether rent review has occurred and the current annual rent rate.
findings.quote: the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date (the "Break Premium"), such payment to be made by way of cleared funds.
findings.uncertainty: Rent rate may have increased due to rent review mechanism in clause 3.2; the exact amount of Break Premium depends on current rent payable. Document establishes initial rent as £850,000 per annum but does not confirm whether reviews have altered the current rate.

findings.title: Break Conditions—Material Breach, Vacant Possession and Payment
findings.interpretation: The tenant's right to exercise a break is subject to three conditions being satisfied on or before the relevant Break Date: (a) no material breach of tenant's covenants remaining unremedied; (b) vacant possession of the whole Premises given to landlord, free from occupiers and subtenants; and (c) Break Premium payment. If any condition is not satisfied, the Break Notice is of no effect and the lease continues.
findings.relevance: These conditions are precedents to successful break exercise. Failure to satisfy any condition will render the break ineffective.
findings.next_step: Do not determine satisfaction of conditions per user instructions. Separately obtain evidence regarding: (i) any current breaches of tenant covenants; (ii) status of any subtenancies or occupiers; (iii) tenant's ability and intention to vacate and pay Break Premium on the Break Date.
findings.quote: The Tenant's right to determine this Lease on a Break Date shall be conditional upon the following conditions being satisfied on or before the relevant Break Date: (a) there is no material breach by the Tenant of any of the Tenant's covenants in this Lease which remains unremedied at the Break Date; (b) the Tenant gives vacant possession of the whole of the Premises to the Landlord on or before the Break Date, free from all occupiers, subtenants and other persons claiming through or under the Tenant; (c) the Tenant pays to the Landlord on or before the Break Date a sum equivalent to six (6) months' rent at the rate payable immediately before the Break Date (the "Break Premium")
findings.uncertainty: Document states conditions but does not identify current position on breaches, occupancy or tenant's ability to comply. Assessment of condition satisfaction requires further facts.

findings.title: Stated Term Expiry
findings.interpretation: The lease is for a fixed term of fifteen (15) years commencing on 1 January 2024 and expiring on 31 December 2038, subject to earlier determination via the break clause or other contractual provisions.
findings.relevance: Establishes the full contractual term and final expiry date absent early break or other termination. Important context for comparing the cost/benefit of early exit via break versus continued performance.
findings.next_step: Confirm whether the current date is prior to 31 December 2038 and assess break dates relative to term expiry.
findings.quote: The Term shall be for a period of fifteen (15) years commencing on 1 January 2024 and expiring on 31 December 2038, subject to earlier determination in accordance with the provisions of this Lease.
findings.uncertainty: Document does not indicate whether the lease has been varied, extended or affected by any other agreement since execution.

findings.title: Initial Rent—£850,000 per Annum
findings.interpretation: The lease specifies an Initial Rent of £850,000 per annum payable by equal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days (25 March, 24 June, 29 September and 25 December). This is the starting rent; it is subject to upward-only rent review at specified intervals.
findings.relevance: Necessary to calculate the Break Premium (6 months' rent). Initial rent is £850,000 p.a., equivalent to approximately £212,500 per quarter or £425,000 for 6 months. However, current Break Premium amount depends on rent payable immediately before the Break Date, which may be higher due to rent reviews.
findings.next_step: Establish the current rent payable under the lease following any rent reviews to date, to calculate the actual Break Premium liability.
findings.quote: The Tenant shall pay to the Landlord the Initial Rent of Eight Hundred and Fifty Thousand Pounds (£850,000) per annum, without any deduction, counterclaim or set-off whatsoever, by equal quarterly payments in advance on the usual quarter days (being 25 March, 24 June, 29 September and 25 December in each year)
findings.uncertainty: Lease history of rent reviews since 1 January 2024 commencement is not provided. Rent review dates and increases must be identified from clause 3.2 and any prior review determinations.
